state.claim: Due to Imran Khan's criticism of Macron's comments on Islam, French authorities cancelled the visas of 183 Pakistani citizens and deported 118 from the country.

candidates.quote: ## Many media reports have surfaced which say that French authorities cancelled visas of 183 Pakistani citizens and deported 118 from the country.All these media reports have used a tweet posted by the username "Consulate General Of Pakistan France", with the handle "@PakConsulateFr". India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that "@PakConsulateFr" is an imposter account of the Pakistani embassy in France.

All these media reports have used a tweet posted by the username "Consulate General Of Pakistan France", with the handle "@PakConsulateFr". The tweet says, "183 visitor visa provided to our citizens has been found to be rejected by french authorities following the criticism by PM Imran khan. 118 citizen with proper documents were deported forcefully. We're currently in touch with french authority to give our citizens temporary stay."
India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that "@PakConsulateFr" is an imposter account of the Pakistani embassy in France. The original Twitter handle is "@PakinFrance".

Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan accused French President Emmanuel Macron on Sunday of "attacking Islam", after the European leader criticised Islamists and defended the publication of cartoons depicting the Prophet Mohammed.
"It is unfortunate that he has chosen to encourage Islamophobia by attacking Islam rather than the terrorists who carry out violence, be it Muslims, White Supremacists or Nazi ideologists."
France has rejected 183 Pakistan visitor visas as per Pakistan Consulate's tweet. Around 120 Pakistanis have been deported by France

passages.P1: # Fact Check: Fake tweet on France deporting Pakistanis go viral after Imran slams Macron
passages.P2: ## Many media reports have surfaced which say that French authorities cancelled visas of 183 Pakistani citizens and deported 118 from the country.All these media reports have used a tweet posted by the username "Consulate General Of Pakistan France", with the handle "@PakConsulateFr". India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that "@PakConsulateFr" is an imposter account of the Pakistani embassy in France.
passages.P8: Tourist visas of 183 Pak citizens were rejected by France after Imran Khan criticised Macron's comments on Islam. Some 118 Pak citizens with proper papers, including a former ISI chief's sister, were deported forcefully.
passages.P10: The tweet posted by "@PakConsulateFr" is an imposter account of the Pakistani embassy in France. The original Twitter handle is "@PakinFrance".
passages.P17: French President Emmanuel Macron has been an outspoken critic of Islamic fundamentalism since the beheading of a teacher in Paris. Countries such as Pakistan and Turkey, in turn, have criticised Macron for his remarks. Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan even accused the French President of encouraging "Islamophobia". And now, news reports say France has come down hard on Pakistani citizens, cancelling tourist visas and forcibly deporting over a hundred in response to the comments.
passages.P20: Many media reports say French authorities cancelled visas of 183 Pakistani citizens and deported 118 from the country. Those deported include the sister of a former ISI chief, the reports say.
passages.P21: All these media reports have used a tweet posted by the username "Consulate General Of Pakistan France", with the handle "@PakConsulateFr". The tweet says, "183 visitor visa provided to our citizens has been found to be rejected by french authorities following the criticism by PM Imran khan. 118 citizen with proper documents were deported forcefully. We're currently in touch with french authority to give our citizens temporary stay."
passages.P22: The same Twitter handle also claimed that France has deported former ISI chief Lt Gen Shuja Pasha's sister.
passages.P23: India Today Anti Fake News War Room (AFWA) has found that "@PakConsulateFr" is an imposter account of the Pakistani embassy in France. The original Twitter handle is "@PakinFrance".
passages.P24: The archived versions of the posts can be seen here, here, here and here. AajTak did the same mistake but later corrected it.
passages.P26:
The Pakistani embassy in France tweeted a screenshot of the imposter account and said it has only one Twitter handle, i.e. "PakinFrance", and anything else claiming to represent the embassy is fake.
> `The Embassy of Pakistan in Paris, France has only one Twitter account @PakInFrance. Any other account claiming to represent the Embassy anywhere in France is fake & misleading & may be reported to @Twitter.@FakeNews_Buster @ForeignOfficePk @MoIB_Official pic.twitter.com/35y7NhXBkh`
> `— Embassy of Pakistan, Paris, France (@PakinFrance) November 1, 2020`
passages.P27: Pakistani media outlets have also reported about the imposter account tweeting misleading information.

S2.title: Pakistan's PM Khan accuses Macron of 'attacking Islam'
S2.retrieval_query: Did Imran Khan publicly criticize Emmanuel Macron's comments on Islam, and what did he say?

passages.P2: # Pakistan's PM Khan accuses Macron of 'attacking Islam'
passages.P7: Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan accused French President Emmanuel Macron on Sunday of "attacking Islam", after the European leader criticised Islamists and defended the publication of cartoons depicting the Prophet Mohammed.
passages.P8: Khan's comments follow statements Macron made last week after a French teacher was beheaded near Paris after he had shown cartoons of the Prophet during a class he was leading on free speech.
passages.P9: Macron said the teacher "was killed because Islamists want our future."
passages.P10: In a series of tweets, Khan said the remark would sow division.
passages.P11: "This is a time when Pres Macron could have put healing touch & denied space to extremists rather than creating further polarisation & marginalisation that inevitably leads to radicalisation," Khan wrote.
passages.P12: "It is unfortunate that he has chosen to encourage Islamophobia by attacking Islam rather than the terrorists who carry out violence, be it Muslims, White Supremacists or Nazi ideologists."
passages.P13: Macron already sparked controversy earlier this month when he said "Islam is a religion that is in crisis all over the world".
passages.P14: The French teacher became the target of an online hate campaign over his choice of lesson material -- the same images that sparked a bloody assault by Islamist gunmen on the offices of satirical magazine Charlie Hebdo, the original publisher, in January 2015.
passages.P15: Caricatures of Mohammed are forbidden by Islam.
passages.P16: Blasphemy is an explosive issue in ultra-conservative Pakistan, where anyone deemed to have insulted Islam or Islamic figures can face the death penalty.
passages.P17: "By attacking Islam, clearly without having any understanding of it, President Macron has attacked & hurt the sentiments of millions of Muslims in Europe & across the world," Khan said.
passages.P18: In an address to the United Nations last month, Khan, a populist leader who has been known to play to Pakistan's hardline religious base, blasted Charlie Hebdo for re-publishing the cartoons, saying "wilful provocations" should be "universally outlawed".
passages.P19: Several Muslim countries have called for a boycott of French goods.
